subject: CloudStitch partner paper — pass-through allocation question
messages:
From: Jenna Park <jenna@cloudstitch.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudStitch Partnerships <partners@cloudstitch.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Partner Paper: CloudStitch Marketplace Addendum - Redlines

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the call last week. We've attached our partner paper with redlines specific to the CloudStitch Marketplace program (see attached: CloudStitch_PartnerPaper_03052027_redlines.docx). Two items we wanted to flag up front:

- Pass-through fee routing: our procurement team is asking that marketplace fees and third-party marketplace levies be passed through to the end-customer rather than being absorbed by CloudStitch or Redwood. They propose the standard pass-through language in Section 5 with no cap.
- Revenue waterfall / commission timing: our finance team would like an explicit monthly reconciliation flow and a 45-day window for invoice disputes.

Can you confirm if Redwood can accept unrestricted pass-through language? If not, please share your counterproposal and any alternative allocation language you typically use with marketplace partners.

Appreciate a quick turn here — we are trying to finalize terms before the marketplace onboarding slated for mid-April.

Best,
Jenna Park
Legal Counsel | CloudStitch
[Attachment: CloudStitch_PartnerPaper_03052027_redlines.docx (docx, 48 KB)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Partner Paper: CloudStitch Marketplace Addendum - Redlines

Marissa / Ben —

Forwarding CloudStitch's redlines (attached) for visibility. Key asks from Jenna: unrestricted pass-through for marketplace levies and a tightened reconciliation window.

Can the sales ops and finance teams live with their timing? If not, what would you prefer we propose?

Kimberly — tagging you for legal input on the pass-through language and any indemnity/ audit implications. Specific asks for legal:
- Acceptability of an uncapped pass-through clause or recommended cap/guardrails
- Recommended timeline for invoice disputes and reasonable audit notice
- Any additional carve-outs we should insist on (e.g., liability cap tied to monthly revenue, carve-outs for third-party payment processors)

Timeline: CloudStitch is pushing to sign before April 15. If we put a compromise in writing by Thursday, I can get this back to them and lock in the onboarding slot.

Thanks —
Soojin
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
[Attachment forwarded: CloudStitch_PartnerPaper_03052027_redlines.docx]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Partner Paper: CloudStitch Marketplace Addendum - Redlines

Soojin / team —

Reviewed CloudStitch's redlines. High-level legal view and recommended compromise below (will prepare tracked redline doc if you want to send a response):

1) Pass-through fee allocation (their proposed "unrestricted" pass-through): not acceptable as written. Risk: open-ended exposure to variable marketplace surcharges (VAT/sales tax, platform fees) could create unpredictable liability for Redwood if the language is ambiguous or if CloudStitch's invoices are late/incorrect.

Recommended language (compromise): allow pass-through of bona fide third-party marketplace levies and government-imposed fees where: (a) the fee is itemized on CloudStitch's customer invoice; (b) Redwood's liability is capped to the amount invoiced to the end-customer for the relevant billing period; and (c) the partner provides reasonably prompt notice of material fee changes.

2) Cap and limitation: propose a soft cap tied to the monthly invoice amount (e.g., pass-throughs may not exceed 4% of the monthly subscription charges for any given invoice) OR explicit carve-out requiring pre-approval for any pass-throughs exceeding that threshold. This preserves commercial predictability while allowing common small platform levies.

3) Reconciliation & dispute window: 60 days for invoice disputes (CloudStitch proposed 45 — we can push to 60 to align with our finance processes). For audit rights, require at least 30 days' notice and limit audits to once per 12 months unless a material discrepancy is found.

4) Indemnity / liability carve-outs: insert a clause that indemnification for third-party fees is limited to direct fees and excludes consequential or punitive damages. Also add a clause that Redwood may withhold commission until disputed items are resolved via the prescribed reconciliation process.

5) Operational hooks: require CloudStitch to provide a monthly pass-through schedule and a point of contact in finance; include an onboarding acceptance checklist tied to the Order Form so we can gate activation until fees are clarified.

If you want, I can create a tracked change version of their partner paper and a short parenthetical comment set for commercial to use in negotiations. Given their timeline, I recommend we propose the compromise language above and offer a one-call exception to discuss any special fees.

-Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Suggested attachments: Redwood_pass-through_template_legal_notes.pdf (3 pages, stub)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Park <jenna@cloudstitch.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partner Paper: CloudStitch Marketplace Addendum - Redlines

Jenna —

Thanks for sending your redlines and for the quick turnaround. We're excited to get CloudStitch live on the Redwood Marketplace. We've reviewed internally and have a proposed compromise attached (Redwood_response_redlines_03192027.docx) and a draft Order Form (Sales_OrderForm_CS-001.pdf) that aligns onboarding milestones to the commercial terms.

Summary of our proposed compromise:
- Pass-throughs: Redwood will accept bona fide third-party marketplace levies and government-imposed fees as pass-throughs provided they are itemized on the invoice and documented in the monthly reconciliation.
- Cap: To keep unit economics predictable, pass-throughs above 4% of the monthly subscription charges require prior written approval from Redwood Finance.
- Disputes: 60-day dispute window for invoice challenges; audits limited to once per year with 30 days' notice (or earlier if material discrepancy).
- Operational: we request CloudStitch assign a finance contact and provide a monthly fee schedule before onboarding activation.

If CloudStitch can accept the attached tracked changes, we'll send a final clean copy and a DocuSign link for execution. Alternatively, we're happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk through the specific clauses. Are you available Monday 3/22 or Tuesday 3/23 for a short sync?

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
[Attachments: Redwood_response_redlines_03192027.docx (docx, 12 KB); Sales_OrderForm_CS-001.pdf (pdf, 45 KB)]
